transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm... just really tired. Um, all the time. It's not just the usual, you know, being a teacher at the end of the day kind of tired. Even if I sleep all night, I just... I have to really force myself to get through grading papers, making dinner, preparing for the next morning. It's just exhausting.
Have you been feeling sad or down most of the time lately?

I suppose... yeah. I mean, most days I can still smile for my students, you know? I get through the lessons fine. But... I don't know, underneath it all, it just feels sort of... flat. Like this gray feeling. It just follows me home, and... even things I usually like, like my garden or my watercolors, they just seem kind of... far away, I guess.
Do you find that you're not enjoying things that you used to enjoy?
I guess... um, yeah. I mean, I kind of just said that. About the garden and the painting. It's just... I don't really do them much right now.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite lately?
Um... no, not really. I think I eat about the same, I guess.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?
Um... no. My sleep is fine. I haven't really noticed any issues with it.
Have you been feeling guilty about anything lately?

Um... I don't know if it's guilt, exactly. Just... I keep thinking I should be handling everything better than I am. Like at work... my lesson plans are taking me twice as long to finish right now. And I had to say no to mentoring a newer teacher. I just... I guess I tell myself I'm letting everyone down. My school, my family. But... yeah.
Have you been having any thoughts about hurting yourself?
No. Um... no, I haven't. Nothing like that.
How long have you been feeling this way?

Um... a while. I think... maybe a little over two years? Like two years and a couple of months. It kind of started around the time... well, my husband stopped working outside the house. Our routine at home just changed, and... yeah. Since around then.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or the opposite, feeling restless and fidgety?
Um... no. I don't think so. I haven't really noticed anything like that.
Have you been feeling anxious or worried about things lately?
Um... no, not really. Just the usual things, I guess. I wouldn't say I've been feeling anxious.
Would you say your symptoms are interfering with your daily life most of the time or just some of the time?

Um... I guess just some of the time. I mean, I'm still working. I still show up for my students, and my family. I just... I don't know. I guess I've pulled back a bit from other things. Like mentoring at school, or going out. I just don't really do the creative things I used to do. But... yeah. I'm still doing what I need to do.
Was there something specific that happened around the time your husband stopped working outside the house that you think might have contributed to how you've been feeling?
Um... no. Not really. I mean, nothing specific happened. It was just... a change, I guess. But I don't think there was a specific event or anything like that.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness or being 'flat' are present nearly every day?

Um... I suppose most days, yeah. I mean, I can still smile for my students... get through the lessons and everything. But... underneath, it just feels like... I don't know, this flat, gray feeling. It kind of just follows me home. And... even my garden or my watercolors, they just... they seem really far away now.
Have you had any periods in the last two years where your symptoms were much worse than they are now?
Um... no, not really. It's just... kind of been the same. Just this steady... sort of feeling. I don't think it's been worse at any point. Just... always there.
Would you say that these feelings of sadness or being 'flat' are present for most of the day or just for a part of the day?
Um... most of the day, I guess. It's just... it's kind of always there in the background.
Would you say that these feelings of sadness or being 'flat' are severe, or more mild and manageable?
Um... more mild, I suppose. It's manageable. I mean... I still get through the day, so... it's not severe.
Have you noticed any changes in your relationships with friends or family members since you started feeling this way?

Um... I don't know if they've changed that much. I mean, I still show up for my family... and my students. But... I guess I've pulled back a little. Just from... extra things. Like mentoring, or going out with friends. And the, um, creative stuff I used to do. Just... keeping things simple, I guess.
Have your symptoms lasted for more than two years?

Um... yeah, I suppose it's been about that long. Maybe... a little over two years. Two years and a couple of months, I think. It kind of started around the time my husband stopped working outside the house... and our routine at home shifted. So... yeah.
Would you describe your feelings of sadness or being 'flat' as significantly impacting your ability to function in daily life?

Um... I don't know about significantly. Like I said... I'm still showing up for my students, and my family. I get the important things done. I've just... pulled back from the extra stuff. The mentoring, going out... the creative things I used to do. Things just don't feel as full anymore, but... I'm still functioning.
Would you say that your symptoms are causing you significant distress?

Um... I don't know if "distress" is the right word. I mean... like I mentioned, I'm still showing up for my students. And my family. I just... I don't do the extra things anymore. The mentoring, or... going out. Or those creative routines I used to have. It's just... quieter now, I guess. But I'm still doing what I have to do.
